acts.title: The Herald's Tablet — IDC
acts.desc: Refugee camp outside Troy's ruins. Idaeus the old herald holds the commission tablet out — the formal document authorizing Priam's last embassy to Achilles. He wants it preserved as an administrative record: proof that Priam went as a king under diplomatic authority, not as a broken old man begging. Insight DC 12.
acts.passText: The Fighter takes the tablet with both hands. Idaeus nods.
acts.failText: The Fighter reaches for it while asking questions about the events. Idaeus pulls it back — not because he won't give it, but because the question misses the point. After a moment's silence, he pushes it forward again.

acts.title: The Herald's Tablet — Perimeter
acts.desc: Greek checkpoint officer wants to catalogue the tablet as war-spoil: Priam's seal belongs to the treasury claim. Argument: a diplomatic commission is not treasury; it was created under Achilles's personal warrior-honor authority; confiscating it retroactively dishonors the truce Achilles made. Persuasion DC 13.
acts.passText: The officer notes the tablet in his log as 'diplomatic record, released under Achilles protocol' and stamps it through.
acts.failText: He holds it for review. A delay of half a day while the officer consults a superior who agrees with the argument the Fighter already made. The tablet is released.

acts.title: The Herald's Tablet — Scaean Gate
acts.desc: Two armed men at the Scaean Gate ruins. Their lord claims a legal honor-debt inheritance from Achilles and wants the commission tablet as evidence. The tablet records a Priam-Achilles transaction, not a Greek-internal dispute; using it in that context destroys its meaning in its correct one. Persuasion DC 14; combat 2× AC 13 HP 16 if failed.
acts.passText: The men step aside.
acts.failText: Combat: two soldiers, AC 13, HP 16 each. The tablet is not damaged — the soldiers were not authorized to destroy it, only to acquire it.

acts.title: The Herald's Tablet — River Ford
acts.desc: A river in early flood has washed out the bridge. The ford is waist-deep. The clay tablet's seal impression can be softened if it soaks; the incised text would survive but the royal seal would blur. Athletics DC 13 to cross without immersion.
acts.passText: The tablet arrives damp on its edges but the seal is intact.
acts.failText: The ford is taken the hard way; the tablet is submerged for a moment. The seal impression is softened. The text is intact. The Archivus will note this — 'seal softened in transit, text fully legible, commission confirmed authentic by content.'

acts.title: The Herald's Tablet — Archive
acts.desc: Archivus Sweelinck receives the tablet, reads the commission text, and files it not under Destruction Events but under Diplomatic Records — Priam of Troy: last known official act. Insight DC 12: understand what he means when he says 'This was the last night Troy was Troy.'
acts.passText: Sweelinck carries the tablet himself to the permanent vault. Before he returns, he says: 'This was the last night Troy was Troy.' The Fighter leaves with nothing material.
acts.failText: Sweelinck files it. He looks at you once. He says nothing. The tablet is in the archive.

acts.title: Helen at the Funeral — Harbor
acts.desc: Troy harbor loading dock. Aethra with a sealed folio — Helen's account of the funeral, composed in her own hand the night before the sack. She is turning back to the refugee line. There is no time for explanation. Insight DC 11: understand quickly enough to accept it.
acts.passText: You take it with both hands. She says: 'She was at the bier. She said those things.' She turns away.
acts.failText: She pushes it into your hands and turns away before you can respond. The folio is in your possession. You know it is Helen's and that it should reach an archive. That is enough.

acts.title: Helen at the Funeral — Checkpoint
acts.desc: The exit checkpoint. The officer wants to log the cedar sleeve as Helen's property under Menelaus's claim. A public speech delivered at a public funeral is not private property. The document records an event. Persuasion DC 12.
acts.passText: He writes 'public speech record, not personal property.' He closes the ledger. You walk through.
acts.failText: He logs it as 'disputed property status, released pending review.' That notation will follow the document. The archive will have to address it.

acts.title: Helen at the Funeral — Steward
acts.desc: Menelaus's household steward's representative on the road, with review authority over Helen's materials. He needs to read it before it's filed. If the household reads it first and decides what 'accurate' means, Helen's voice arrives filtered. Persuasion DC 13.
acts.passText: You name the category: public record, delivered before thousands at a state funeral, not subject to household review under any Greek precedent. He knows this is correct. He turns his horse.
acts.failText: He rides beside you for half a mile, asking questions about the content without reading the folio. He is noting your answers. He eventually turns back. The folio is intact.

acts.title: Helen at the Funeral — Ambush
acts.desc: Three hired men above the road. The hard faction wants the folio gone entirely. They do not want to review it. They want it to not exist. Combat 2× hired men AC 12 HP 20.
acts.passText: Both men are down. The cedar sleeve is intact. The seal is unbroken.
acts.failText: They take the cedar sleeve. But they didn't count the folios before taking it — the account and Aethra's covering note are on separate sheets. You still have the account, wrapped in your own pack.

acts.title: Helen at the Funeral — Archive
acts.desc: The archive. Establish the chain of custody from Helen's hand to yours without a gap: Helen wrote it the night of the funeral; gave it to Aethra; Aethra gave it to you at the harbor. Insight DC 11.
acts.passText: The archivist says: 'Chain is intact.' She opens the primary accounts section of the ledger. She writes Helen's name in the compiler field. 'Helen of Troy' — using the Trojan name, not the Greek one. She closes the ledger.
acts.failText: Filed as 'attributed statement, provenance established by carrier, classification pending secondary review.' It is in the archive. Helen's name is in the record.

acts.title: The Embassy's Offer — Unsigned List
acts.desc: Refugee camp. Idaeus has kept the unsigned offer list from the Book 9 embassy — the formal gift list Odysseus carried to Achilles that was carried back unsigned after the refusal. It documents both what was offered and its rejection. History DC 11: understand why an unsigned offer document is an active record.
acts.passText: You understand. He nods. 'Take it with the tablet,' he says. 'They belong together.'
acts.failText: You carry the record without grasping the legal argument. Idaeus summarizes it while you pack.

acts.title: The Embassy's Offer — Inheritance Clerk
acts.desc: Greek camp road. A legal clerk processing estates wants to classify the unsigned document as evidence of a pending claim against Agamemnon's heirs. The document is not a legal instrument; it is an archival record. Persuasion DC 12.
acts.passText: He accepts the neutrality argument. He files a request with the archive for future access.
acts.failText: He files an administrative notice that the document is under claim. You continue; the notice follows the document to the archive.

acts.title: The Embassy's Offer — Achilles's Heirs
acts.desc: Constantinople. Achilles's heirs want the document certified as an acknowledgment of debt by Agamemnon that passes to themselves. The document records a transaction; it does not adjudicate the debt. Insight DC 12.
acts.passText: They accept the carrier/interpreter distinction. One of them says: 'At least the record will be there.' You say: yes.
acts.failText: They follow for two hours. You eventually name an archive scholar they can consult after filing. They accept.

acts.title: The Embassy's Offer — Mountain Faction
acts.desc: Mountain road cliff section. An Agamemnon estate faction tries to force you to the cliff edge to acquire the document. Athletics DC 13.
acts.passText: You take the wider path and the cliff section passes without incident. They abandon the follow.
acts.failText: They force you close to the edge. The record stays with you. They follow no further but the road is watched.

acts.title: The Embassy's Offer — Archive
acts.desc: Weimar archive intake. File the unsigned offer list beside the Herald's Tablet. The archive holds both the offer and the refusal — the acknowledged debt and the terms — without adjudicating between them.
acts.passText: Sweelinck files it beside the Herald's Tablet. He says: 'Achilles was honest about what he wanted. Agamemnon was honest about what he'd pay. The record has both.' He closes the register.
acts.failText: Filed under the Trojan cycle. The offer is in the archive. The refusal is noted.

acts.title: Patroclus's Commission — Charioteer's Record
acts.desc: Refugee camp. Automedon, Achilles's charioteer, wrote the commission tablet the evening after the battle — the exact words of Achilles's instruction to Patroclus. The limit instruction and the glory comment are both recorded. Insight DC 11: understand the completeness argument before he explains it.
acts.passText: You grasp the completeness argument. Automedon hands you the tablet without comment.
acts.failText: You carry the tablet. Automedon adds a brief note explaining the tablet's circumstances.

acts.title: Patroclus's Commission — Achilles's Heir
acts.desc: Road toward Ragusa. Achilles's heir intercepts you — he wants the glory comment removed from the record. The carrier cannot characterize the tablet's contents; it goes as written. Persuasion DC 12.
acts.passText: He accepts that the carrier cannot characterize the tablet's contents. He turns back.
acts.failText: He asks you to describe what you observed of Automedon's state when he handed over the tablet. You describe it neutrally. He notes this and turns back.

acts.title: Patroclus's Commission — The Nestor Problem
acts.desc: Ragusa. A scholar has a competing account from Nestor that contradicts Automedon's version of what the commission said. The archival record can note both; the commission tablet is a first-hand field document regardless. Insight DC 12.
acts.passText: He accepts the separation of historical artifact from philological argument. He says he will send the Nestor transcription to the archive separately.
acts.failText: He argues for thirty minutes before accepting that the carrier cannot settle competing witness accounts. He gives you a copy of the Nestor transcription to carry alongside the tablet. You carry both.

acts.title: Patroclus's Commission — The Patroclus Family
acts.desc: Road north. Patroclus's surviving aunt waits at the waystation. She needs to know whether the tablet records what Achilles said or what Patroclus decided. Insight DC 11: understand what she actually needs before she finishes asking.
acts.passText: You say: the tablet is what Achilles said. It doesn't say what Patroclus decided. She closes her eyes for a moment. She lets you pass.
acts.failText: You tell her the tablet records the commission, not the decision. She thanks you and sits down at the roadside.

acts.title: Patroclus's Commission — Archive
acts.desc: Weimar archive intake. File Patroclus's commission tablet. The archive holds the exact words as they were said — not as either family needs them to have been said.
acts.passText: Sweelinck files it. He reads both entries — the limit instruction and the glory comment — and marks the section: 'Complete commission record. Both instructions present.' He closes the vault.
acts.failText: Filed under the Patroclus record. The commission is in the archive.

acts.title: Andromache's Loom — What Chrysis Kept
acts.desc: Troy harbor. Chrysis, Andromache's household slave, holds the half-finished purple weaving she cut from the loom before the room burned — dropped shuttle still attached. She cannot take it to wherever she is being assigned. Insight DC 11: receive it correctly.
acts.passText: You take it with both hands and say nothing. She looks at you for a moment. She nods.
acts.failText: You say something inadequate. She hands it over anyway. She looks away.

acts.title: Andromache's Loom — Inventory Officer
acts.desc: Harbor checkpoint. A Greek inventory officer wants to log the weaving as assessable textile property. The cloth is an interrupted cultural record, not an assessable item — the interruption in the weave at the moment of Hector's death is the content. Persuasion DC 12.
acts.passText: He accepts the archive distinction. He notes: 'cultural record, non-assessable, archive transit.'
acts.failText: He logs it as 'purple textile, incomplete, origin Troy, status disputed.' You argue for release on archive transit; he grants a provisional release with the notation following the cloth.

acts.title: Andromache's Loom — The Greek Woman
acts.desc: Adriatic coast road. A Greek woman whose own weaving was destroyed in the sack wants the cloth returned to Troy — or to the nearest equivalent. The archive is the nearest equivalent to a place where things are kept as they were. Insight DC 12.
acts.passText: You explain the archive as the form of return. She accepts it. She says: 'Tell them whose cloth it was.'
acts.failText: She argues about it for a while. You explain the archive's preservation role. She eventually agrees, though unhappily.

acts.title: Andromache's Loom — Weavers' Guild
acts.desc: Visby. The weavers' guild wants to examine the cloth for provenance documentation. The guild's interest is technical; the archive's interest is contextual — the two are not the same classification. Persuasion DC 11.
acts.passText: He accepts the archive document distinction. He asks if the archive would accept a guild technical report as supplementary material. You say: write to Weimar.
acts.failText: He brings his two colleagues. They examine it for one day. They are careful. The cloth is returned intact with three technical observations added to the carrier's bundle.

acts.title: Andromache's Loom — Archive
acts.desc: Weimar archive intake. File Andromache's unfinished weaving — the dropped shuttle still attached to the last thread. The weft line at the break is exact: the moment of interruption visible in the weave.
acts.passText: Sweelinck examines the shuttle still attached to the thread. He says: 'The moment is in the weave. We can read when she stopped.' He carries it to the textile vault himself.
acts.failText: Filed under Andromache of Troy, household effects. The cloth is in the archive.

acts.title: The Shield's Description — Bronze Attendant
acts.desc: Scaean Gate ruins. The Bronze Attendant — a self-moving mechanical figure made by Hephaestus — holds a scroll describing the shield of Achilles from Book 18. The attendant's instruction was to find an archive; it has been standing here waiting. History DC 12: understand the dual context — what Hephaestus made versus what the shield recorded.
acts.passText: You understand the dual context. The bronze attendant's instruction was to find an archive, not to explain.
acts.failText: You carry the scroll without the full context. At the archive, Sweelinck asks you how you acquired it and from whom. You describe the bronze attendant. He writes it down.

acts.title: The Shield's Description — Philosopher of Crafts
acts.desc: Road north. A Greek philosopher of crafts wants to classify the scroll as a work of aesthetic theory — the shield described as art, not as a weapon. The two contexts are inseparable; the world depicted on a weapon is not decoration. Persuasion DC 12.
acts.passText: He accepts the inseparability argument. He says: 'The world on a weapon is not decoration. You're right.'
acts.failText: He argues the aesthetic primacy at length and eventually agrees that the archive can cross-file. He asks for the archive's address.

acts.title: The Shield's Description — Ajax Estate
acts.desc: Constantinople. An Ajax estate legal representative wants the shield description classified as composition evidence in an inheritance dispute. The scroll's composition predates any possession claim; the archive holds it as a creation record. Insight DC 12.
acts.passText: He accepts the composition/possession distinction. He notes the archive destination and withdraws.
acts.failText: The representative follows to the next waystation arguing about the composition evidence being relevant to the provenance claim. Eventually he accepts that composition pre-dates possession.

acts.title: The Shield's Description — River Crossing
acts.desc: Danube tributary flood crossing. The copper scroll has a wax seal that must stay dry. Athletics DC 12 to carry it above the water.
acts.passText: The scroll crosses dry. The seal is perfect.
acts.failText: One hand drops. The wax seal takes water contact. At the archive, Sweelinck examines the seal and notes: 'The bronze attendant's impression is partially damaged; the text is intact.' He files it.

acts.title: The Shield's Description — Archive
acts.desc: Weimar archive intake. File the copper scroll — the full ekphrasis of Achilles's shield as Hephaestus made it: five layers, two cities, the harvest, the ocean at the edge.
acts.passText: Sweelinck reads the scroll in silence. He sets it down. 'The world as it was before the war,' he says. 'And a weapon.' He files it under both categories.
acts.failText: Filed under Achilles's armor, related documents. The scroll is in the archive.

acts.title: Hecuba's Supplication — Myrine's Hands
acts.desc: Scaean Gate ruins. Myrine, a Trojan woman who carried Hecuba's gold-figured robe from the burning temple, holds it out — both hands burned from the carrying. The robe was the supplication gift Hecuba brought to Athena's statue before Hector went out to fight. Religion DC 11: understand the divine-side argument before she explains.
acts.passText: You understand the divine-side argument before she explains. She looks at you once and says: 'She was there when we laid it on the statue's knees.' You say: I understand.
acts.failText: You carry the robe. Myrine adds a note describing the circumstances of the supplication and the robe's removal from the temple.

acts.title: Hecuba's Supplication — Temple Inventory
acts.desc: Scaean Gate road checkpoint. A Greek temple inventory officer wants to log the robe as disputed temple property under Athena's dedications. The robe was offered in supplication, not given permanently; the goddess refused the supplication; the dedicatory status is paradoxical. Persuasion DC 13.
acts.passText: He accepts the paradox argument. He notes: 'dedicatory offering in contested status, archive transit authorized.'
acts.failText: He notes it as 'disputed temple property, Trojan origin, Athena dedication' and issues a transit document. You continue with the document attached.

acts.title: Hecuba's Supplication — Priestess Theano
acts.desc: Rome. The priestess Theano — who handed the robe to the statue in the poem — wants to carry the robe to the archive herself and deliver it in Hecuba's name. The custody chain has a gap if she joins. Insight DC 12.
acts.passText: You explain the custody chain's integrity. She accepts it. She asks if her name can be in the archive's record of the supplication. You say: write to Weimar.
acts.failText: She takes the robe and agrees to carry it to the archive. You accompany her. The chain arrives with the gap noted.

acts.title: Hecuba's Supplication — Religious Commission
acts.desc: Alpine road. A Roman religious commission representative claims the robe falls under the standard commission for temple property. The robe's unique status — offered in supplication, refused by the goddess — falls outside the commission's ordinary category. Persuasion DC 12.
acts.passText: He accepts that the robe's unique status falls outside the commission's category. He notes: 'offering in unresolved dedicatory status, commission authority does not apply.'
acts.failText: He flags the argument as novel and sends a message to Rome for clarification. He does not stop you — the argument is strong enough to release — but the flag follows you.

acts.title: Hecuba's Supplication — Archive
acts.desc: Weimar archive intake. File Hecuba's gold-figured robe — singed at one corner from the burning. The robe that the goddess refused. The supplication that was not accepted. The archive will hold both the offering and the refusal.
acts.passText: Sweelinck receives the robe with both hands. He reads Myrine's note. 'Hecuba offered this before Hector went out,' he says. 'The goddess did not prevent what followed.' He files it under Supplications — Refused. First entry.
acts.failText: Filed under Hecuba of Troy, religious documents. The robe is in the archive.

acts.title: Apollo's Account — Servant at Tenedos
acts.desc: Tenedos approach. A sanctuary servant holds the Plague Tally Tablet — an ivory document recording Apollo's plague in sequence: the god struck mules first, then dogs, then men. Religion DC 12: understand the mule-to-dog-to-man sequence before he explains.
acts.passText: He explains the mule-to-dog-to-man sequence before you ask. 'The god worked in order,' he says. 'He always did.' He writes a second note explaining the progression. You receive the Plague Tally Tablet.
acts.failText: He gives you the tablet with a note saying only: nine days, Chryse. The category sequence is unmarked.

acts.title: Apollo's Account — Physicians' Descendants
acts.desc: Ilium district. Physicians' descendants want the tablet as a medical record — the plague as a case study in epidemic progression. The tablet records a divine action in sequence, not a wound pattern; the classification matters because the archive can hold both the divine cause and the human consequence. Insight DC 12.
acts.passText: They accept the classification distinction and release it without copying. One of them says: 'The god is the better physician. We only treat what he leaves behind.'
acts.failText: They make a copy of the tablet before releasing it, noting the mule-to-man sequence as a symptom-progression document. The copy stays with them; the original continues.

acts.title: Apollo's Account — The Chryses Question
acts.desc: Constantinople. A Byzantine scholar disputes the interpretation: was the plague an act of wrath or an act of reciprocity? The tablet records nine days and a sequence; the ambiguity between wrath and reciprocity is not a flaw in the record but its value. History DC 13.
acts.passText: He accepts that the ambiguity is the document's value. He writes: Apollo — Chryse — nine days: divine procedure, cause unresolved between wrath and reciprocity.
acts.failText: He writes a marginal note on the tablet's linen wrapping: reciprocity, not wrath. The note travels with it.

acts.title: Apollo's Account — Mountain Road
acts.desc: Alpine road. Rockfall camp. The ivory tablet must be protected from impact damage. Athletics DC 14.
acts.passText: The tablet arrives intact and dry. The linen wrapping is clean.
acts.failText: The tablet survives but the wrapping tears; a corner of the ivory chips. The damage is cosmetic; the text is intact. Sweelinck will note the chip.

acts.title: Apollo's Account — Archive
acts.desc: Weimar archive intake. File the Plague Tally Tablet — nine days, the god's procedure recorded in sequence.
acts.passText: Sweelinck reads the tablet. He sets it down. 'Divine procedure, cause unresolved,' he says. 'We will file it that way.' He opens a new category heading: Divine Actions — Sequence Records.
acts.failText: Filed under Apollo, plague records. The tally is in the archive.

acts.title: Dolon's Report — The Tamarisk
acts.desc: Edge of no-man's-land. A Myrmidon scribe holds the intelligence strip — Dolon's report given in exchange for a promised ransom, recorded verbatim. Dolon's information was accurate; he was killed on completion. Insight DC 12: understand the voluntary exchange structure.
acts.passText: You understand the voluntary exchange structure before he explains it. He gives you the strip and says: 'He was accurate about everything. The horses were exactly where he said.'
acts.failText: You carry the strip with a note: Dolon, Trojan scout; information given in exchange for promised ransom; killed on completion; intelligence confirmed accurate at dawn.

acts.title: Dolon's Report — Thracian Survivors
acts.desc: Trojan harbor. Thracian survivors want the strip destroyed — their king Rhesus was killed the same night based on Dolon's intelligence, and they do not want his name in the archive. The strip can note 'the Thracian king, unnamed at his survivors' request.' Persuasion DC 13.
acts.passText: They accept the argument. One of them says: 'He would have fought well the next morning.' You say nothing. He nods and lets you pass.
acts.failText: They make you swear not to name Rhesus by name in the archive entry. You agree. The entry will read: the Thracian king, unnamed at his survivors' request.

acts.title: Dolon's Report — Catalogue Keeper
acts.desc: Constantinople. A Doloneia authenticity scholar believes Book X was added late to the Iliad and wants the strip suppressed as it would complicate his hypothesis. A field document predates composition disputes. History DC 12.
acts.passText: He accepts the separation of historical artifact from philological argument. He writes: field document, Book X parallel; authenticity question separate.
acts.failText: He adds a note to the strip's linen wrapping: possibly late addition; Doloneia authenticity disputed. The note travels with it.

acts.title: Dolon's Report — River Crossing
acts.desc: Danube flood crossing. The ox-hide strip's final line — he had not yet fought; this was his first night — will blur if the lower fold takes water. Athletics DC 14.
acts.passText: The strip crosses dry. All text is intact.
acts.failText: One hand drops briefly. The lower fold takes water; the last line blurs slightly. The intelligence is readable but the final line requires inference. Sweelinck will note the blur.

acts.title: Dolon's Report — Archive
acts.desc: Weimar archive intake. File Dolon's intelligence strip — the voluntary exchange, the accurate report, the first night.
acts.passText: Sweelinck reads the final line. 'He had not yet fought,' he says quietly. He files it under Intelligence Records — Single Exchange. He does not name Rhesus.
acts.failText: Filed under the Trojan cycle, intelligence records. The strip is in the archive.

acts.title: The Stripped Inventory — Armorer's Record
acts.desc: Battlefield morning. An armorer holds the clay inventory — the list of Achilles's divine armor as Hephaestus made it, assembled piece by piece, stripped from Patroclus's body and put on Hector. History DC 12: understand the theological chain — the god's gift, the loan, the stripping.
acts.passText: You understand the theological chain before he explains it. He adds one line to the reverse in your presence: the god made it the night before the war.
acts.failText: You take it with a note: inventory of Achilles's armor, stripped from Patroclus, now on Hector. Provenance noted briefly.

acts.title: The Stripped Inventory — Andromache at the Loom
acts.desc: Upper Troy ruins. Andromache sees the inventory tablet — she recognized the armor on Hector the morning he went out and knew it was not his. She holds the tablet for a moment. Insight DC 12.
acts.passText: She sets it in your hands and turns back to the loom. 'He will die in that armor,' she says. 'Tell them that.' You write it on the back of the wrapping.
acts.failText: She holds the tablet for an hour before returning it. Her handprint, in clay-dust, is on its surface. It stays there.

acts.title: The Stripped Inventory — Arms Dealer
acts.desc: Constantinople. An arms dealer wants the inventory as a title deed establishing a claim to the divine armor or its equivalent value. The tablet is a commission record, not a deed of gift. Persuasion DC 12.
acts.passText: He accepts the gift-vs.-commission distinction and concedes the legal claim fails. 'A good try,' he says. 'Come back if you find the actual armor.'
acts.failText: He makes a sketch of the inventory's contents — the listed pieces — for his own files. The tablet continues.

acts.title: The Stripped Inventory — The Blind Spot
acts.desc: Trojan harbor. A fisherman who watched from the walls testifies that the armor looked wrong on Hector — 'not too large. Just wrong.' The phenomenological observation belongs in the archive alongside the inventory. Perception DC 12.
acts.passText: You identify the phenomenological category before he finishes speaking. He nods: 'Yes. That's the word. Wrong. Not too large. Just wrong.'
acts.failText: You write his testimony on a scrap and tuck it inside the tablet's wrapping: witness says the armor looked wrong on him. He moved differently.

acts.title: The Stripped Inventory — Archive
acts.desc: Weimar archive intake. File the stripped inventory — the divine armor's full component list, the god's gift, the loan, the stripping, and the fisherman's testimony that it looked wrong on him.
acts.passText: Sweelinck reads Andromache's note on the reverse. He reads it twice. He files it under the inventory entry: Witness note — Andromache, wife of Hector: he will die in that armor. He closes the catalog.
acts.failText: Filed under Achilles's armor, inventory. The record is in the archive.

acts.title: Priam's Ransom — Herald's Manifest
acts.desc: Troy courtyard. Idaeus holds the ransom manifest — the full list of what Priam loaded on the mule cart to ransom Hector's body: twelve robes, twelve mantles, the measured gold. He weighed the gold himself. None of the sons was allowed to help. Persuasion DC 12.
acts.passText: He understands you understand. He folds it carefully, the way you fold something important, and says: 'He weighed the gold himself. None of the sons was allowed to help.'
acts.failText: He gives you the manifest with a note: items carried by Priam son of Laomedon to the tent of Achilles; Hector's body returned in exchange.

acts.title: Priam's Ransom — Hecuba's Objection
acts.desc: Troy palace ruins. Hecuba wants her dissent in the record — she advised against the journey; Priam went regardless. She will dictate it herself. Insight DC 12: receive the dictation in the form she intends.
acts.passText: She dictates one sentence: I told him not to go. He went. You write it at the bottom of the manifest in a new hand. She approves it.
acts.failText: She dictates a long paragraph; you write a summary: Hecuba advised against the journey; Priam went regardless; she gave him wine.

acts.title: Priam's Ransom — Achaean Inventory Officer
acts.desc: Greek camp commissariat. An inventory officer wants to reconcile the ransom manifest with the official Achaean property records. A ransom is a negotiated exchange; the cup Achilles gave Priam was divine guest-friendship, not inventory. History DC 12.
acts.passText: He accepts the divine-arrangement argument and releases the manifest without annotation. He notes in his own record: no reconciliation possible; divine escort classified.
acts.failText: He notes in his record that the Thracian cup passed without inspection and inserts a gap in his manifest. The official record will show a discrepancy. The papyrus continues unaltered.

acts.title: Priam's Ransom — Achilles's Table
acts.desc: Constantinople. A hospitality scholar wants to reclassify the ransom as guest-gifts — the meal Achilles gave Priam, the truce, the escort. The ransom was a ransom; the hospitality followed after. Persuasion DC 13.
acts.passText: He accepts the temporal sequence argument. He writes: ransom document; hospitality context noted but classification unchanged.
acts.failText: He writes a marginal note on the papyrus wrapping: see also: xenia transformation; hospitality context disputed. The note travels with it.

acts.title: Priam's Ransom — Archive
acts.desc: Weimar archive intake. File the ransom manifest — everything Priam loaded, the gold weighed, and Hecuba's one-line dissent at the bottom in a different hand.
acts.passText: Sweelinck reads Hecuba's line at the bottom. He reads it again. He files it under Priam's entry: 'Ransom complete. Hecuba's dissent noted in original hand. Classification: act of a father, not a king.' He closes the register.
acts.failText: Filed under Priam of Troy, diplomatic records. The manifest is in the archive.

acts.title: Thetis at the Sea-Floor — Rock at Tenedos
acts.desc: Tenedos shore. A Nereid stands in the shallows holding a bronze cylinder sealed with silver — Thetis's own record of Achilles's arc: his birth foreknown to end in early death, his choice to accept it, her grief held silently through the war. Religion DC 14: name all four elements of Thetis's arc in order to receive it.
acts.passText: You name all four in order. The Nereid comes one step out of the water, sets the cylinder in your hands, and goes back. She does not speak again.
acts.failText: You get two elements of four. She gives you the cylinder anyway, with a look that says you got the important ones. 'She mourned first,' the Nereid says. 'That's the part men always forget.'

acts.title: Thetis at the Sea-Floor — Night in the Tent
acts.desc: Achilles's tent site. An old Myrmidon soldier wants the arc of the cylinder explained — specifically the night Thetis came to mourn with Achilles after Patroclus died. He needs to understand what she knew then. Insight DC 12.
acts.passText: You describe the full arc from Thetis's record without opening the cylinder. He nods slowly. 'He always knew,' he says. 'That's the thing. He always knew.'
acts.failText: You read him the last entry from the cylinder: He is buried with Patroclus's bones in the golden urn I brought from Olympus. I gave it to him when he was young. He did not know what it was for. He sits down on the ground.

acts.title: Thetis at the Sea-Floor — Golden Urn Question
acts.desc: Constantinople. A collector wants the cylinder as authentication for a fragment he claims is part of the golden urn. The cylinder authenticates the urn's existence; it does not authenticate his fragment. Persuasion DC 13.
acts.passText: He accepts the authentication argument and raises his cup. 'A reasonable position. The archive has its standards.' He does not press further.
acts.failText: He photographs the cylinder's exterior — the sea-glazing, the silver-foot seal — and notes that it matches known Nereid artifact typology. This note circulates. The cylinder continues.

acts.title: Thetis at the Sea-Floor — Road North
acts.desc: Frozen river crossing. The ice is thin at center. The bronze cylinder must be kept above the water. Athletics DC 15.
acts.passText: The Fighter reads the ice correctly and crosses without breaking through. The cylinder arrives cold and dry and sealed.
acts.failText: The ice gives at the center; the Fighter goes in to the waist; the cylinder is held above water; Thetis's record stays dry but the Fighter arrives at Weimar half-frozen. Sweelinck opens the door and says nothing for a moment.

acts.title: Thetis at the Sea-Floor — Archive
acts.desc: Weimar archive intake. File Thetis's cylinder — the mother's record of the son she knew would die young, held through the whole war. The last ATH document. The archive holds what the war did not destroy.
acts.passText: Sweelinck receives the cylinder. He does not open it. He reads the exterior inscription: Thetis, daughter of Nereus, for Achilles, son of Peleus. He sets it in the permanent vault. He says: 'The war is over. The archive is not.' He closes the vault door.
acts.failText: Filed under Thetis, divine records. The cylinder is in the archive. The ATH chain is complete.
